entries.postTitle: How to Stop Avoiding Hard Decisions

captions.threads:
1/4 There's a decision you've been carrying. Not thinking about, not considering, but literally carrying it on your shoulders like a weight that's become so familiar you stopped noticing it was there. Weeks. Maybe months. You know exactly what it is.

2/4 The avoidance isn't laziness. It's not confusion either. It's protection. Your nervous system learned long ago that choosing means losing something, disappointing someone, or admitting you were wrong about a direction you chose before. So you wait. You gather more information that doesn't matter. You ask people whose opinions shouldn't matter. You make the decision feel bigger and scarier than it actually is.

3/4 But here's what actually happens when you delay: the decision doesn't get lighter. It metastasizes. It bleeds into your creative work, your relationships, your sleep. It becomes self-betrayal dressed up as caution. And every day you don't choose, you're choosing anyway, just passively.

4/4 The hard decisions aren't hard because they're complex. They're hard because choosing anything means accepting that you can't have it all, and that some version of you dies in the process. That version was probably already dying anyway. https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/how-to-stop-avoiding-hard-decisions
